sasha: Quick summary from today

sasha: Ran a focused KV prefix priming comparison — replay harness vs synthetic traffic. Results look noisy but there's a measurable regression when we enable the new kernel selector + aggressive batching heuristics.

sasha: High-level numbers: replay hitrate ~ 62%, synthetic hitrate ~ 70%. P99 latency increased ~12ms on the replay run with kernel=auto and batching=aggressive.

nate: oof. can you paste the exact commands you ran?

sasha: Sure. Replay run (prod trace, 64 concurrency):

```bash
./replay --trace traces/2025-prod-prefixes.json --concurrency 64 --kernel-selector auto --batching aggressive --kv-enable-prefix true --warmup 120
```

sasha: Synthetic run used workload-gen with same mean seq len, but synthetic uses a uniform seed distribution. Command:

```bash
./workload-gen --model vicuna-13b --qps 500 --seq-distribution file:seq-hist.json --kernel-selector fallback --batching balanced --kv-enable-prefix true
```

maria: Important callout: the replay trace has a higher tail of long prefixes from a small number of customers (big chat threads). That changes kernel code path selection (longer kv lookups + different attention window) so kernel-selector auto tends to pick the 'large-seq' kernels more often.

aj: Did you capture KV cache metrics (warmup curve / eviction counts) during the runs?

sasha: Yep. From metrics: replay run: initial hitrate 15% -> 62% after 3m; eviction spikes at minute 1 and 4. Synthetic: warmup 28% -> 70% steady, almost no eviction spikes. Eviction events correlate with kernel swap windows.

perf-bot: [artifact] flamegraph: s3://perf-artifacts/1850004321/replay-flame.svg
perf-bot: [artifact] metrics: s3://perf-artifacts/1850004321/kv-metrics.csv

nate: Could be a correctness/concurrency race too — eviction during a long prefix read might be dropping KV shards mid-request, causing retries and kernel fallback. Any evidence of retries or fallback events?

sasha: Logs show ~0.3% 'kv-miss-after-lock' events and ~0.1% 'kernel-fallback' events timed with eviction spikes. I've pasted the relevant log snippet: 

```
[00:01:13] shard-23 evict start id=0x7f4b
[00:01:13] request 0x9ab3 read-prefix shard-23 -> miss (locked-while-copy)
[00:01:13] request 0x9ab3 kernel-fallback -> small-seq-kernel
```

sam: Nice repro. Two hypotheses: (1) kernel-selector auto is too eager and causes extra kernel swaps under realistic prefix skew; (2) aggressive batching increases KV hold times leading to eviction races.

aj: For apples-to-apples we should force the same kernel on both replay + synthetic and run with/without aggressive batching. Also add a run with KV prewarm enabled (prefix prefetch warmup step) to measure delta.

sasha: Agreed. Proposed matrix (each row x 3 seeds):
- kernel=fallback, batching=balanced, kv-prewarm=off
- kernel=fallback, batching=balanced, kv-prewarm=on
- kernel=auto, batching=balanced, kv-prewarm=off
- kernel=auto, batching=aggressive, kv-prewarm=off

maria: Also include a targeted concurrency sweep: 8, 32, 64, 128. The eviction behavior looks sharply worse at 64+ in replay.

nate: One measurement nit: warmup windows need to be long enough for steady-state — use at least 5 minutes of sustained load and drop first 2 minutes from metrics. Otherwise sampling bias kills comparisons.

aj: Agreed. And record per-request kernel id, KV hit flag, and per-shard eviction timestamp so we can correlate. Minimal schema:
`{ts, req_id, kernel_id, kv_hit, shard_id, eviction_ts, latency_ms}`

sam: If we see repeated 'locked-while-copy' misses, we should consider bumping the copy lock hold-time metric or switching to copy-on-read for hot prefixes. But only after we verify it's actually the contention culprit.

sasha: Next steps I'm going to run the matrix tomorrow morning (timestamps: 1850040000-1850043600 UTC). Will attach artifacts and a short DAG of which runs correspond to which config.

maria: If the kernel selector is the main driver, maybe we need a hybrid policy: kernel selector uses a per-prefix heuristic plus a short cool-down to avoid thrashing on transient long-seq bursts.

nate: Also add one synthetic where we inject a small number (~0.5%) of very long prefixes to mimic the heavy tail. That should help isolate whether skew explains everything.

aj: Perfect. If you want I can wire an alert to catch kernel-fallback rate >0.05% so we spot regressions early in CI.

sasha: Thanks all — I'll post results and the run manifest here. :thumbsup:
